findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() has confusing, inverted-looking dead logic that always returns false
No test coverage added to assert SQL expressions remain disabled regardless of feature flag
findings.body: The whole point of this PR is to make `QueryTypeSQL` always fail with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', including when `FlagSqlExpressions` is toggled on, in order to close CVE-2024-9264. No test was added (or updated) in this diff to lock in that behavior — e.g. a test that enables `FlagSqlExpressions` via a feature-toggle test double and asserts `ReadQuery` still returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL`. Without such a regression test, a future refactor of `enableSqlExpressions` (see the dead/inverted logic noted separately) could silently re-enable the vulnerable code path and nothing in CI would catch it.

findings.title: Stub DB implementation has no tests verifying it always errors
findings.body: `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` replaces the real DuckDB-backed implementation with a stub whose `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` methods unconditionally return `errors.New("not implemented")`. This is the second line of defense against the vulnerability (independent of the feature-flag gate in reader.go), but there are no unit tests asserting these methods always fail, nor any test exercising `sql.TablesList`/`SQLCommand.Execute` end-to-end to confirm no code path can execute arbitrary SQL/filesystem access anymore. Given this is a direct mitigation for a critical CVE, this logic should be explicitly covered by tests rather than relying on incidental callers getting an error.

findings.title: Error message is misleading about why SQL expressions are unavailable
findings.body: The error returned when `QueryTypeSQL` is requested — `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` — is factually inaccurate: SQL expressions are implemented but intentionally disabled for security reasons (per the PR description, this is a hard-disable to close CVE-2024-9264), and the feature flag `FlagSqlExpressions` still exists and can be toggled with no effect. Returning a message implying the feature doesn't exist yet (rather than that it is disabled) can confuse users/operators who previously relied on it, and conflicts with any surviving documentation that still describes the flag as functional.
